source_documents.title: Anti-Kasha's Rule Emissive Switching Induced by Intermolecular H-bonding

conditions_studied: organic solvents with and without water

reference_evidence_units.quote: The emitter initially gives rise to an S3-to-S0 dominant emission as indicated by our experimental and theoretical studies.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA

reference_evidence_units.quote: On this basis, it can be toggled into an S2-to-S0 dominant emission upon the H-bond formation between the triformyl groups and water molecules.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA
reference_evidence_units.statement: Water H-bonding switches the emitting state to S2.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Overall, the photophysical switching arises from stabilization of the CT
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA
reference_evidence_units.statement: The switch comes from stabilising a CT excited state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: thus to effectively regulate the distribution of the π-π* and n-π* electronic transitions as well as the corresponding radiative decay efficiency.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA
reference_evidence_units.statement: H-bonding reorders ππ*/nπ* states and their radiative efficiency.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The “electronic” effect of Hbonding is here more pronounced than its rigidity effect as indicated by the current photophysical studies.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TA

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Stabilisation of a CT excited state by polar solvent/water drives the emission switch.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: H-bonding redistributes the ππ*/nπ* state order and the radiative efficiency of the emitting higher states.
